clauses.current_legal_basis: The held U.S. Code (Office of the Law Revision Counsel release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints Executive Order 13239 as a note to 26 U.S.C. 112 with no ending statement; the order's own text has no end date or condition; and the bounded searches of the U.S. Code, the eCFR and the Federal Register executive-order catalog located no later order revoking, superseding or terminating the designation. Laws enacted after October 9, 2026 and on or before October 14, 2026 are not reflected in the held U.S. Code edition.
clauses.reason: The order designates Afghanistan, including the airspace above, as an area in which Armed Forces of the United States are and have been engaged in combat for purposes of section 112 of the Internal Revenue Code, and designates September 19, 2001 as the commencement date of combatant activities. Its text states no end date, expiry condition or termination mechanism, and no held later instrument ends it, so on the evidence held the designation was still in force on October 14, 2026.

research_rationale:
EO 13239 of December 12, 2001 (66 FR 64907, FR Doc. 01-31119) was read in full from the held Federal Register text; it has one operative command in two sentences. Acting under section 112 of the Internal Revenue Code (26 U.S.C. 112), the President designated Afghanistan, including the airspace above, as an area in which Armed Forces of the United States are and have been engaged in combat, and designated September 19, 2001 as the date of commencement of combatant activities. The text has no end date, no expiry condition and no review step. The bounded searches recorded below found no instrument that revokes, supersedes, terminates or amends the order: the Office of the Federal Register disposition-note search and the saved-text search returned no hit, the eCFR search returned no hit, and the U.S. Code search found one hit, the note to 26 U.S.C. 112 that prints the order text with no ending statement. The only other held text naming the order is a Federal Register rule document (FR Doc. 2010-24360, 75 FR 59968, September 29, 2010) that cites Executive Order 13239 among theater-of-operations designations; it recites the order and neither amends nor ends it, so it is not a later event. The held catalog observation for the order has an empty note, which supports neither continuity nor an end; the YES conclusion rests on the order's own terms and the searches. The U.S. Code edition held is release point 119-121, current through October 9, 2026; laws enacted from October 10 to October 14, 2026 are not reflected in it.

savings.reason: The order is operative, so no savings question arises from an ending; the order contains no savings clause, and no held later instrument ends it or preserves residual effects. The U.S. Code note that prints the order contains no ending statement.
